test_name: Arm paint missing on dropped and respawned mech arms - dcaa3ed1-085f-4fdf-ab30-0bdb6d094259
summary: Passed: after the player died twice in the editor, the dropped arms kept their paint once the dead mech was removed, and every respawned mech's arms were painted. The dropped arm was still listed as part of the dead mech's paint, so when the dead mech was cleaned up it wiped the paint off the arm too, and only the dying player has that cleanup step. The respawned arm could miss its paint when the saved paint loaded before the arm was built. Now a detached arm leaves the mech's paint list, and arms built later get the paint that was already applied.
instructions:
TASK: missing arm paint after player dies

DESCRIPTION:
when a player gets killed and his arm falls to the ground, the player who just died sees that his arm on the ground has no paint(does have polish), while any other player sees that the arm on the ground does have paint, but the respawned mech's arm do not have paint.

REQUEST (from Amit):
@Big Sys okay well then dispatch the junior dev if you haven't already, find the cause, implement and fix

Big Sys read the card, the code and the tracker first. Her hand-off: Two separate bugs under Assets/__Multiplayer/Scripts/Mech/Paintshop/ — read that folder's CLAUDE.md and .claude/guides/systems/multiplayer/paintshop.md first (PropertyBlockMaterialSwapper invariants, PaintRendererSet as sole paint writer).

BUG 1 — dying player sees own dropped arm unpainted (others see it painted): PaintshopCompositor.OnDisable() calls ClearOutputTextures() -> PaintRendererSet.ClearTextures, which unconditionally zeroes _WhiteParams (and _ColorTex/_SurfaceTex) on every Cover slot of the ROOT PaintRendererSet's merged arrays (PaintRendererSet.cs ~147-149, via TryMergeIntoParentSet ~193 the arm renderers are merged into this root set). On death the arm detaches (MP_MechArm.Detach(), ~line 1418) and becomes debris that outlives the mech; when the mech itself is torn down (on respawn) the compositor's OnDisable/Teardown fires and strips paint off the now-orphaned debris renderers too. Only the owning client ever had a PaintshopCompositor (remotes get it stripped in MP_PlayerMech.ThrottledSetup via PaintTextureSynchronizer.StripPaintshopRuntimeFromMech, ~line 752) — that's why only the dying player sees it, not remote viewers. Polish survives because it's owned separately by PropertyBlockMaterialSwapper and ClearTextures never touches it.
Fix: in MP_MechArm.Detach(), remove the detached arm's renderers from the root PaintRendererSet's tracked arrays (so ClearTextures on mech teardown can no longer reach them) OR make PaintshopCompositor.Teardown/ClearOutputTextures skip renderers that no longer belong to a live mech (filter by GameEntity/parent check before clearing).

BUG 2 — respawned mech's arm has no paint (separate bug): PaintTextureSynchronizer.OnReadyForUse -> DownloadAndApplyAsync -> ApplyToMech applies the color/surface textures to the root PaintRendererSet once. On first spawn the S3 fetch is slow enough that arm setup finishes first. On respawn, PaintTextureCloudProvider.DownloadAsync hits the local PaintTextureDiskCache (sync File.ReadAllBytes, ~line 132) and returns same-frame — before MP_PlayerMech.InitializeSetup/SetupArms (~line 1403) has created the arms and merged their PaintRendererSets into root (TryMergeIntoParentSet). So the apply lands on a root set that doesn't have the arm renderers in it yet, and never gets reapplied after the merge.
Fix: cache the last-applied (color, surface) on PaintRendererSet (set in ApplyTextures), and have TryMergeIntoParentSet re-push the parent's cached textures onto newly-merged children when a merge happens after the initial apply — mirrors the existing parent.PushOutputRT() call at PaintshopCompositor.cs ~491.

Not a cause: the auto-attached commit on the card (LocalRemoteValue: use remote values on the local mech when viewed from outside its bubble) — checked, LocalRemoteValue<T> usage in this codebase is cockpit-tilt/shake config only, unrelated to paint. Don't chase it.

Repro to verify the fix: kill a mech, have the dying player look at their own dropped arm (should now show paint, not just polish) while another player also looks at it; then let that player respawn and check the new mech's arm has paint immediately. Report back to Omer/Amit on the card with repro confirmation once verified, since Omer asked for a more detailed repro earlier in the thread.

EXTRA (from the card):
- Commit 48d9c77694 (one-hamsa/underdogs): LocalRemoteValue: use remote values on the local mech when viewed from outside its bubble — https://github.com/one-hamsa/underdogs/commit/48d9c7769479c5be73ee3ccdba031bf3ebabaff1 - Not the cause of this bug (confirmed by Big Sys): LocalRemoteValue<T> in this codebase is only used for cockpit-tilt/shake config, unrelated to paint - do not chase this commit.
Big Sys's hand-off (from reading the card, code and tracker) identifies two separate bugs under Assets/__Multiplayer/Scripts/Mech/Paintshop/: (1) PaintshopCompositor.OnDisable -> ClearOutputTextures/PaintRendererSet.ClearTextures strips paint from the detached arm debris because it's still tracked in the root PaintRendererSet's merged arrays when the mech tears down on respawn; fix by removing detached arm renderers from the root set in MP_MechArm.Detach(), or by filtering Teardown/ClearOutputTextures to skip renderers no longer belonging to a live mech. (2) On respawn, PaintTextureCloudProvider.DownloadAsync returns same-frame from the local disk cache, so PaintTextureSynchronizer applies textures to the root PaintRendererSet before MP_PlayerMech.SetupArms has merged the arm renderers in via TryMergeIntoParentSet, so the arm never gets the paint; fix by caching last-applied (color, surface) on PaintRendererSet and re-pushing it onto newly-merged children in TryMergeIntoParentSet (mirrors PaintshopCompositor.cs ~491 PushOutputRT call). Read that folder's CLAUDE.md and .claude/guides/systems/multiplayer/paintshop.md first (PropertyBlockMaterialSwapper invariants, PaintRendererSet as sole paint writer) before starting. Omer asked earlier in the thread for a more detailed repro/video since he was unsure it reproduces consistently - report back to Omer/Amit on the card with repro confirmation once verified, using the repro steps Big Sys provided: kill a mech, have the dying player look at their own dropped arm (should show paint not just polish) while another player also looks at it, then let that player respawn and check the new mech's arm has paint immediately.
